items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: But when I first met him, it was like I’d known him for years... And that’s how our relationship, from that day, it was perfect. He was really, really, really wonderful.

ctx.x: Well this could be a hard question, but how do you price your work?

That is difficult. Because like I say, I am a novice so I really feel I can’t do it. Because I’m slow. It takes me time. Although if they give me a timeline, that helps. Because now I say well this is a chunk of time in order for me to do this. I ask some friends, and I look © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

at — sometimes I look at some published charts and how much they are charging for the chart itself, and then I say well okay — and I may ask them what kind of budget that you have, and we can discuss it. Because I think it’s just like my performing. Everything’s on sliding scale as far as I’m concerned. And here again I realize they’re asking me now to write something and I would like to be paid as much money as I can possibly get paid. items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: But like Milton Hinton, he said if a young woman wanted to play, he could care less if you are a girl, blue, green, purple.

ctx.x: How important is it that students learn about the parts of being a musician that aren’t just the music. Punctuality and personality. As a matter of fact I think you summed it up “hanging on the bandstand” I think was your —

Well, you know I really want — if the players really want it, it’s here for them. There is a lot of talk about, I mean just here at the conference, there aren’t a whole lot of minority kids here. So that’s kind of disconcerting to a point. But like Milton Hinton, he said if a young woman wanted to play, he could care less if you are a girl, blue, green, purple. If you wanted to play and you wanted to learn something from him, it’s yours. Whatever you’ve got is yours. And I feel the same way. The music knows no…
Right. If they had kept quiet you’d have just kept doing it.
